instruments.evidence: Read what the client gets past the limit: 429 with code RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, X-RateLimit-* headers and Retry-After 60; and what the page did with it: onError handled only 403 and 404, so a refused send vanished with nothing on screen (finding fe-silent-429).

axios 1.18 sets error.status from response.status (AxiosError.js:136), and api.ts rejects the axios error unchanged apart from the 401 refresh, so the helper reads a real status.

The test router copies the limiter wiring from cmd/server by hand; main() builds its routes inline and routes_test.go cannot reach them, so no test can see cmd/server drop a limiter. Recorded as a known limit of the guard.

instruments.evidence: The limiter's per-user read (userID.(int)) falls back to the IP bucket on any other type; the claims type is int, checked.

The per-IP test first used X-Forwarded-For on a request with no RemoteAddr, which gin ignores, so both IPs shared one bucket and the test failed; it now sets RemoteAddr, the address gin really reads from an unknown client.
